excerpt: UPL Cp 9 (CES 26 1) is a registered cowpea variety. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1989. It takes about 45 days from sowing to the first harvest, with 9.05 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about UPL Cp 9 (CES 26 1) cowpea
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

UPL Cp 9 (CES 26 1) cowpea takes about 45 days from sowing to the first harvest. That is 8.3 days faster than the average of the 13 cowpea varieties with a day count, 53.3 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 9.05 t/ha beats the average of its group, 5.44. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: The pests and diseases that hit cowpea fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its pods grew about 19.8 cm long. A hundred seeds weigh about 14.1 grams, so the higher this number, the bigger the seed. The seed coat is green.
Where and when to plant UPL Cp 9 (CES 26 1) cowpea

Cowpea fits the dry season after rice, on the moisture the paddy keeps. Pick by use: green pods for vegetables, or dry seed. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).
